extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO disciplinary officers, and attorneys subject to USPTO professional conduct rules
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and criteria the USPTO uses to evaluate practitioner conduct and impose discipline (e.g., failure to inform clients, neglect, dishonesty), plus the types of sanctions and mitigating/aggravating factors considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to inform client of important Office correspondence (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a),(b) via 10.23(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes failure to inform a client of important Office correspondence when the correspondence (i) could have a significant effect on a matter pending before the Office, (ii) was received by the practitioner on behalf of a client or former client, and (iii) was such that a reasonable practitioner would believe under the circumstances that the client or former client should be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples/manifestation: not informing clients of Office correspondence, allowing applications to become abandoned without client knowledge or consent, failing to notify client of notices of abandonment. In this matter, respondent did not inform Clients #1–#4 of important Office correspondence and allowed abandonments without client knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4); 11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes engaging in dishonest, fraudulent, deceitful, or otherwise misrepresentative conduct in connection with practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples/manifestation: misrepresenting status of patent applications to clients. The Final Order cites respondent's false statements about application status to Client #1 and Client #4 as violations of these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowingly giving false or misleading information to a client in connection with business before the Office (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a),(b) via 10.23(c)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes knowingly providing false or misleading information to a client related to business before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from facts: falsely informing Client #1 that her application was proceeding normally when it had been abandoned. Such knowingly false assurances violate this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect of legal matters entrusted to a practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes neglect of legal matters entrusted to a practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manifestations include failing to respond to Office communications, failing to pursue prosecution, and allowing patent and trademark applications to become abandoned without client knowledge or consent (as occurred for Clients #2, #3, and #4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failing to seek lawful objectives of the client and prejudicing/damaging a client (37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes failing to seek a client's lawful objectives and engaging in conduct that prejudices or damages a client during the professional relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: not responding timely to Office correspondence and allowing abandonments that prejudiced client rights (stated as a violation based on respondent's conduct).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to provide competent representation; failure to act with reasonable diligence and promptness (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101 and 11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must provide competent representation and act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office found respondent violated these duties by failing to promptly reply to Office correspondence and allowing patent and trademark applications to become abandoned (noted especially for conduct after May 3, 2013).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to reasonably consult with client and to keep client reasonably informed (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.104(a)(2) and (a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires reasonable consultation with the client about means to accomplish objectives and keeping the client reasonably informed about the status of a matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: not informing Client #4 about a notice of abandonment issued after May 3, 2013. The rule was applied where respondent failed to consult and failed to keep clients informed of material status changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions and remedial measures (suspension, limited recognition, reinstatement procedures, dissociation, publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms of discipline and procedural steps the Office may order: suspension from practice, limited recognition for narrow purposes, conditions on reinstatement, dissociation from USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates, publication of Final Order and notice in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific sanctions in this matter: two-year suspension from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters; limited recognition for 60 days solely to facilitate compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b); dissociation of respondent's name from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates; prohibition on applying for a Customer Number until reinstated; OED to publish the Final Order in OED's FOIA Reading Room and a materially consistent notice in the Official Gazette. The OED Director must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors considered in determining discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors the Office may consider to mitigate discipline, as noted in the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In mitigation the OED considered: (i) no prior disciplinary history during 40 years of registration; (ii) respondent's expression of remorse; (iii) respondent attempted to mitigate harm by reviving some patent applications at his own expense; and (iv) respondent fully cooperated with OED during the investigation. These mitigators were cited as justification in imposing the specific sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings (aggravating/ rebuttal/consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of a disciplinary proceeding in future matters against the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the Office may use this record (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of same/similar misconduct; (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding against respondent as an aggravating factor and/or to rebut statements made on respondent's behalf; and (3) in connection with any request for reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
